newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees to harmonise consumer credit calculation.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees to harmonise consumer credit calculation.

text.p: European Union consumers ministers agreed in principle on Monday on a plan to harmonise at European Union level the way consumer credit is calculated.
A final decision must wait for the opinion of the European Parliament, which is expected early in 1997.
The aim of the system is to harmonise the method used to calculate the Annual Percentage Rate of Charge.
Current disparities mean that consumers can find it difficult to find out which credit offer is cheaper.
"This will enable consumers to compare, with greater certainty and confidence, the credit products available throughout the EU," Ireland's Consumer Minister Pat Rabbitte said in a statement.
Under the agreement the result of the calculation will be expressed with the accuracy of at least one decimal place.
The intervals between dates used in the calculations will be expressed in years or in fractions of a year with a year being 365 days, 365.25 days or, in the case of a leap year, 366 days long.
A month will be presumed to have 30.41666 days. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
